item.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation Will Let You Spec Into Different FITS Classes But Still Wear The Party's Classic Outfits
item.description:
One of the bigger additions to Square Enix's Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy in the upcoming finale, Revelation, is the FITS system. This Function-Integrated Tactical Suitwear system allows players to spec Cloud and friends into four different "types," which are basically jobs. There's Warrior, Knight, Black Mage, and Summoner. The feature adds additional customization to Revelation's already feature-packed combat (which also adds two new party members with Cid Highwind and Vincent Valentine), but it also changes how a party member is dressed. After going hands-on with Final Fantasy VII Revelation's first chapter during Tokyo Game Show last week – read my preview here – I asked director Naoki Hamaguchi if players can still wear the team's classic outfits. 

While I enjoy different costumes and outfits in games, if there is a canon outfit, I always prefer to wear it during big story moments. When fighting Sephiroth, I want Cloud wearing his classic Soldier gear – not the flowing dress outfit associated with a FITS type like the Black Mage, for example. Hamaguchi quickly quells my fears, telling me, "That was really important for us to keep." 

"There are, of course, players who want to use all these different classes, but still want to keep Cloud and his signature look," Hamaguchi says, explaining that this option will be available from the jump. 

It's not quite clear whether it's an official transmog system or just an option to turn FITS looks on/off, but it's still great to hear I can take a Black Mage Cloud into a fight against Sephiroth while still wearing Cloud's trademark Soldier gear. 

Final Fantasy VII Revelation hits PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, and PC next year on April 8. 

In the meantime, read my Final Fantasy VII Revelation – Chapter 4 preview, and then check out my Final Fantasy VII Revelation – Chapter 1 preview. After that, read about how Final Fantasy VII Revelation will have four different performance modes on PS5 Pro.

item.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation Will Have Four Performance Modes On PS5 Pro
item.description:
I got hands-on with Final Fantasy VII Revelation at Tokyo Game Show last week, playing about 25 minutes of the game's first chapter. You can read more about my experience during that preview here, including what's happening narratively and my thoughts on the game's FITS system, but I also spoke with Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi about the PlayStation 5 Pro's graphics settings available in this build. Before hopping into the game, I paged through the visual settings and noticed "Quality," "Performance – Sharp," and "Performance – Soft." 

It's clear Quality mode aims for the highest resolution and might run at a locked 30 FPS (though I couldn't confirm that during my preview). The Performance – Sharp and Performance – Soft return from post-launch Final Fantasy VII Rebirth support, giving players options for how they want to experience 60 FPS gameplay on PS5 Pro. Similar to Rebirth, Revelation's Performance – Smooth features a 60 FPS framerate with smoother, or softer, image quality, while Performance – Sharp features a 60 FPS framerate with sharper image quality. As for what that will look like in the final game, more testing beyond a 25-minute demo is needed, but the game was beautiful when I played it and ran at a consistent 60 FPS. 

Hamaguchi tells me players will see differences between these modes in things like hair, environmental detailing, shading, and more, however. 

On X during TGS, Hamaguchi posted that the PS5 Pro will leverage PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) to deliver a mode that features both 4K image quality and 60 FPS gameplay, though he didn't say what it's called. Unfortunately, I can't recall seeing this option in the game's settings – blame it on TGS memory or perhaps it wasn't available in this preview build.

I should note that, because this build was playable on PS5 Pro, there's no word on which of these modes, if any, will be available on base PS5, but if it's like Rebirth, all three, sans the PSSR mode, will be playable. 

Final Fantasy VII Revelation launches on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, and PC on April 8, 2027.

item.title: Xbox Lays Off 268 More People, Hands Halo Series To Activision
item.description:
Earlier this year, Xbox performed a massive wave of layoffs, eliminating 1,600 roles and sharing that more cuts would come soon. Today, those cuts have come: Xbox has announced it is laying off 268 roles across its first-party studios, XGS management, and central functions layer. Halo Studios in particular has been significantly impacted, and today's announcement states that Activision will take over development for the next Halo title.

The news broke via an Xbox Wire post called "Continuing Our Reset," by Xbox executive vice president and chief content officer Matt Booty. It makes three major points. First, it lays out the layoffs and says the company is "roughly three-quarters of the way through previously announced restructuring."

Next, he announces some internal studio restructuring. Activision will expand its remit to World's Edge (known for Age of Empires) and Rare (known for Sea of Thieves), and a new team will be created within Activision to develop the next Halo title. Meanwhile, a "small team at Halo Studios will continue supporting the Halo community and games in-market." This last part is huge news – the makers of Call of Duty are now also in charge of Halo. It's perhaps the clearest example of how massive studio mergers can ultimately stifle competition – the two series hailed as the pillars of the first-person shooter are now being made under the same roof.

Other studios are also getting shuffled around. You can read Booty's breakdown verbatim below:

  • Bethesda will expand its remit to include Obsidian, which will continue its current projects, including Grounded, as well as the new Fallout project made in collaboration with Bethesda Game Studios.

  • King will expand its remit to include Microsoft Casual Games, uniting our two global leaders in casual game design and live operations.

  • Playground and Turn 10 will come together as one studio focused on the Forza and Fable franchises. These two studios have been creative and franchise partners for over a decade, and today’s changes will formally move their work into one team.

The final note details Xbox's studio divestitures, which it announced a few months back. Compulsion and Double Fine have officially spun off to run independently, and Undead Labs has a deal with a new publisher, but will still release State of Decay 3 on Game Pass when it launches next year. On the other hand, "two separate agreements for Ninja Theory fell through," and Xbox will begin consultations on a proposed closure. Arkane is in a similar position, though Booty says those consultations are expected to last "through the end of the year."

The news is unfortunate across the board, but the cuts to the Halo team are especially impactful. Halo: Campaign Evolved was one of our most recent cover stories, and we enjoyed the final product at launch, but it seems to have done little to hold off Xbox's all-encompassing waves of cuts. Meanwhile, Halo's original creators at Bungie also laid off "most of" the Destiny 2 team, though Bungie also recently announced plans to bring back vaulted Destiny 2 content.

item.title: Bungie Announces Plans To Restore Vaulted Destiny 2 Content And Substantial Reworks To Marathon
item.description:
It’s been a few months since Bungie ceased active development of Destiny 2, bringing the game’s nine-year lifecycle to an abrupt end and angering many players in the process. Bungie has heard and responded to this outcry by obliging one of the biggest fan requests for Destiny 2. The studio is also sharing plans to evolve its well-received but tepidly performing extraction shooter, Marathon. 

In a developer video and studio blog post, Bungie studio heads Poria Torkan and Josh Deane acknowledge the fanbase’s resentment and plans to earn back player trust. 

Bungie has been creating games for over 30 years and we have welcomed the communities that have formed around them. Over the last few years, we lost sight of that, and there have been real consequences. We lost trust, we lost incredible colleagues, and we lost sight of what we should be prioritizing most, our players.

As a new leadership team, we must own that.

We aren’t just listening to feedback, we understand your disappointment. We are not asking you to trust what we say today. We know that trust must be earned through the quality of our games, the decisions we make, and how consistently we show up for our players.

To this end, Bungie plans to restore Destiny 2 content archived in the game’s digital Vault. This means vaulted campaigns, destinations, and raids will become available for all players again. “We understand that removing these experiences had a lasting impact on player trust and enjoyment of Destiny,” reads Bungie’s blog post. “Destiny 2 is more than just the content itself. It is a place where players have built memories together, formed lasting friendships, and shared experiences that have stayed with them for years. We cannot change the decision we made, but we can acknowledge its impact and do the work to make it right by restoring these important parts of Destiny’s history.”

However, Bungie notes that years of updates to Destiny 2 have fundamentally changed the game, so bringing back vaulted content will require work to make them compatible with the current version of Destiny 2. For example, vaulted content will require updated lighting, combat encounters, combatants, and other renovations, which Bungie explains will take time. The studio promises to keep players updated on its progress in the coming months.

Bungie states unvaulting content is "the first step to lay the foundation for how we reforge into new stories and games that you all deserve." Whether this takes the form of Destiny 3 or other projects remains to be seen, but the studio is not walking away from this universe just yet. 

As for Marathon,  Bungie reiterates that while the game is an important part of its future, it was never meant to replace Destiny 2. The studio acknowledges Marathon "did not reach as many players as we had hoped" and that it needs to evolve. To this end, it has announced plans to expand it to “a deeper survival experience.” 

“Through the remainder of Marathon’s first year, we will continue strengthening its combat, world, and competitive tension while giving players more agency in how they engage with the game,” Bungie says. “That means creating meaningful experiences whether you prefer cooperative PvE, competitive PvP, or the unpredictable tension of Marathon PvPvE."

Bungie states it wants to work with the community to improve and expand Marathon to fit several playstyles. It also states it still has many things planned for the October Nightfall Refresh and December Symbiosis updates. More updates regarding Marathon will be shared later this week. 

2026 has been a challenging year for Bungie. Marathon arrived in March to a generally positive critical reception (here's our review), but as Bungie acknowledges, it has not retained the player numbers the studio hoped for. This has only intensified following the end of Destiny 2, as some fans blamed Marathon's existence for the studio moving on from Destiny 2. To make matters worse, with Destiny 2 coming to an end, Bungie laid off most of that game's development team. With Bungie addressing these realities head-on, it will be interesting to see if these proposed updates bring back lapsed fans of both games.

item.title: The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – September 18, 2026
item.description:
We are hard at work this week on putting the finishing touches on our next issue, which we will be revealing soon. Did you know we put out a printed magazine and you can actually have it sent to your home by going to gameinformer.com/subscribe? That is a service we happily provide. But that's not all that is happening this week. Blizzcon happened. Big video games like Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave and Marvel's Wolverine came out, and I went and saw the new Resident Evil movie. It's very good! But you're here to learn about what new video games you should play this weekend. Before that, though, here are some of the biggest stories of the week.

  • Blizzard Announces World Of Warcraft: Forever, Expanding Vanilla WoW With New Zones, Raids, 1,000 New Quests
  • More Than Anything, Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil Movie Understands How It Feels To Play A Resident Evil Game
  • Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Review - Let The Games Begin
  • Control Resonant – Review In Progress
  • Bill Skarsgård Cast As The Lead In Physint, Kojima's Metal Gear Solid Spiritual Successor
  • Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter Review - A Superb Sequel

Some other new games that released this week worth checking out that we don't have full entries for below? Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter, RuneScape: Dragonwilds, and Aniimo are all now available, and the Crazy Taxi-inspired Truck-kun is Supporting Me From Another World?! is now on Switch 2. But check out our more thorough list below.

Marvel’s Wolverine

Matt Miller

Insomniac’s latest superhero adventure is a very different beast from the studio’s earlier work on the Spider-Man games. Like the character named in the title, this new game is a fast-moving, furious, intense ride, virtually from start to finish. Insomniac has focused on a rollercoaster ride of an action experience, and some other things, like story and exploration, take a back seat to ensuring that intense focus on battle always remains front and center. But if you’re in the mood for crazy, bloody fights, memorable bosses, and big set-piece encounters, Wolverine delivers. Check out our full review for more.

Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave

Eric Van Allen

The latest Fire Emblem hits Switch 2 this week, and if anyone closes out the titanic hour count of Fortune's Weave by Monday morning, please consider grass and the benefits of touching it. Seriously, though, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is a mammoth of a strategy RPG, filled with narrative yarns to unravel, charming units to recruit, dungeons to delve into, and Heroic Games to conquer. No matter how many RPGs are available at any given time on a Nintendo console, Fire Emblem hits certain parts of the palate that few other series can; it's a special blend of strategy and role-playing, a strong blend of in-unit relationships and army building, a dash of humor and a heavy helping of deeper lore. Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is a smorgasbord of all that and more, and you certainly won't hurt for ways to fill your weekend hours with it. My pro-tips for players picking it up: Kalla's Blessing is incredibly powerful; get an Archer and a Pegasus Knight as soon as you can; do all the sidequests you can manage. You can read my full review here.

Resident Evil (2026)

Kyle Hilliard

Resident Evil from Zach Cregger, the director/writer behind the critically acclaimed horror movies Barbarian (2022) and Weapons (2025), released last night and I liked it a whole lot. If you're looking for a film adaptation featuring characters and story from the universe of the Resident Evil video games, you might be disappointed. The references to Resident Evil lore are few and instead the movie focuses on a normal guy who basically gets stuck in a Resident Evil video game. Sure, we know how Leon, Claire, and others respond to Umbrella's shenanigans, but what about the guy who was just trying to deliver an organ to a hospital when everything went to hell?

The result is a movie that expertly captures the feeling of playing a Resident Evil game. Cregger is clearly a fan of the games and the result is a shocking and shockingly funny movie that I am already considering trying to see again before it leaves theatres. I recommend going to see it with a crowd if you can.

SoulQuest

Matt Miller

After an earlier release on PC, SoulQuest has now made its way over to Switch 2/Switch. The pixel-art action game is relatively straightforward on its surface, but as the game ramps up in intensity, there’s a lot of fun in maintaining your combo with your various skills and juggling whole squads of enemies to increase your score for each encounter. The story seems to draw equally from Celtic mythology and anime narrative and visual cues. For players looking for a button-mashy good time that gradually translates as you play into something a bit more sophisticated, it could be just the ticket.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight on Switch 2

Charles Harte
I'm a Lego fan, a Batman fan, and a Lego Batman fan, so it's not surprising I'm a big fan of Legacy of the Dark Knight, and I'm happy it met my high expectations. While the game launched in May, there are three new reasons to check it out today. First, its paid DLC just dropped, giving players a new level and Mayhem Mode to experience as The Joker and Harley Quinn. Legacy of the Dark Knight has far fewer characters than most of TT Games' previous work, so new options are a big deal. There's also a free update dropping today that adds the Absolute difficulty, making a very easy game one step more difficult. The lack of challenge was one of my main let-downs, so this is encouraging. Finally, Legacy of the Dark Knight also drops on the Switch 2. While I haven't played that specific version, I'm glad it's appearing on another platform, giving more people (kids especially) an avenue to check out the rain-slick streets of Lego Gotham. For my full thoughts, you can check out my review.

Absolum on Switch 2

Matt Miller

The celebrated roguelite brawler (one of my personal favorites from 2025) has just been released on Switch 2. If you’ve yet to dig in and enjoy the unique characters and many potential upgrades, now is a great time to give it a shot. The art style is gorgeous, and the many paths players can take through a given run gradually pull back the curtain on some lovely fantasy world-building. There’s also crossplay support in case you want to enjoy the included 2-player mayhem with a buddy on a different platform.

Tabletop Pick – Pop Art

Matt Miller

Published by Road to Infamy Games, and themed around the classic pop art movement (think Andy Warhol’s Campbell’s Soup Can series), this fascinating drafting and tableau-building game uses a mix of colored background cards and transparent cards you can lay on top.

When stacked together, a new visual emerges, which is then scored around particular objectives, such as using more objects than your opponent or having more portraits or particular colors in one of your rows. The dynamic that emerges is one of a light puzzle game, as you seek to display your cards in a way that maximizes your score; doing this creates a display that mimics the feel of an art gallery you’ve curated. Pop Art is distinct and clever, and a good pick if you’ve been looking for something a bit different.

item.title: Hyper Light Drifter Maker Heart Machine Lays Off 'Nearly Everyone'
item.description:
Heart Machine, an indie developer known for games like Hyper Light Drifter and Solar Ash, has laid off most of its staff, according to studio head Alx Preston. Preston took to LinkedIn to share the news that the studio was working on a game that was funded by an unnamed publisher, but after that publisher dropped out this week, Heart Machine didn't have the resources to keep its staff onboard.

Preston doesn't indicate that the studio will shut down, however, simply stating "I’m not sure yet what’s next for Heart Machine to survive. However, we'll keep pushing to build a path while we are still here."

Here's Preston's full statement.

I have very difficult news today.

We had been working on an unannounced title, funded by a publisher. This week, they decided to no longer move forward with it. Without this key income for the studio, any other immediate prospects or other funds, nearly everyone at the studio had to be laid off. It's devastating.

Everyone will be provided with as much support as possible, including assisting with placement. If you know of any roles for extraordinarily talented, kind people, please reach out and we will coordinate.

Thank you so so much to all of the incredible people who contributed their efforts and talents to making amazing things at the studio. Thank you to our amazing community and fans.

Navigating an increasingly challenging industry has been extremely difficult, and I’m not sure yet what’s next for Heart Machine to survive. However, we'll keep pushing to build a path while we are still here.

Heart Machine came onto the scene in 2016 with Hyper Light Drifter, which was self-published and funded by a Kickstarter that raised over $600,000. We loved it, scoring it a 9.5 in our review. Its following game, Solar Ash did well, but made less of a splash. Hyper Light Breaker, Heart Machine's 3D multiplayer roguelike follow-up to Hyper Light Drifter, launched in early access in 2025 to relatively negative reviews. After layoffs in October 2025, that game's development ended, and it never got a proper 1.0 release. Most recently, it put out a Metroidvania called Possessor(s), which currently has a 71 on Metacritic, but that launch was preceded by a second wave of layoffs, also in October of 2025. You can read Game Informer's Possessor(s) review at the link. Taking place just under a year later, today's layoffs feel like one more nail in Heart Machine's proverbial coffin.

Being an indie studio is hard right now. Just this year, Oxenfree developer Night School Studio, Wanderstop developer Ivy Road, and Moss developer Polyarc all shut down.

item.title: Bill Skarsgård Cast As The Lead In Physint, Kojima's Metal Gear Solid Spiritual Successor
item.description:
Physint, an upcoming game from Kojima Productions, just found its star. The game is set to be a spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid, a game series Hideo Kojima famously led for many years before parting ways with Konami, which holds the rights to the IP to this day. In 2015, Kojima founded Kojima Productions to make games on his own terms, and Physint is one of those projects. It's still in the early stages, so we don't know much, but today the studio revealed it's got a big name attached to the project; Bill Skarsgård will play the game's lead. You can take a look at the actor being photographed for a teaser photoshoot below.

 

Bill Skarsgård is best known for his role as Pennywise the clown in the most recent duology of It movies, but also appeared as Count Orlok in 2024's Nosferatu and the scheming Marquis Vincent de Gramont in John Wick 4. 

Kojima is quoted in a press release published alongside the news. “I'm delighted to confirm the lead role for PHYSINT will be Bill Skarsgård,” said Hideo Kojima. “We are both long-time fans of each other’s work, and we've decided to embark on this new adventure together. The costume fittings, scans, and camera tests we conducted with Bill and Charlee earlier this year gave me tremendous confidence in the direction of the project.”

The "Charlee" that Kojima references is Charlee Fraser (Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga, Anyone But You),  who was confirmed for the game alongside actors Ma Dong-seok AKA Don Lee (Train to Busan, Eternals), and Minami Hamabe (Godzilla Minus One) last September.

Physint was originally revealed as a PlayStation-published game, but in a dramatic turn of events, PlayStation recently dropped out of the project.  A report from Bloomberg claims that Kojima Productions had missed key deadlines and was on track to be "well over budget," and that sales for the Death Stranding series hadn't met PlayStation's revenue expectations. That same day, Xbox was revealed as the game's new publisher, hence Kojima's appearance in the video above, which closed out Xbox's Tokyo Game Show presentation.

Xbox and Kojima Productions were already partnered to release OD – Knock, a game starring Sophia Lillis and Hunter Shafer. Kojima's Physint update above is preceded by some new behind-the-scenes footage of recent OD – Knock performance capture sessions.

item.title: Here's How To Get A Steam Frame, Valve's VR Headset, And How Much It Costs
item.description:
Valve's new VR headset, the Steam Frame, is dropping very soon, and today is the first day you can sign up to purchase one of your own. Much like with the launch of the Steam Machine, the console-like PC that dropped earlier this year, today is the first day you can get added to a randomized list to be selected to purchase a headset of your own. Sign-ups are available now and will be live for 72 hours, ending at 1:00 PM ET on September 17. 

"We found the reservation system to be helpful with the launch of Steam Machine by improving the purchase experience and limiting resellers, and are implementing it once again for Steam Frame," Valve stated in a press release. It's nice that the practice seemingly limits scalpers (the bane of any tech-buyer in the 2020s), but it is a shame that the process is partially left up to luck. Valve says the first wave of customers will be notified starting on September 18.

The Steam Frame is a wireless VR headset that allows you to play VR and non-VR games on Steam. It comes with two Steam Frame controllers, one for each hand, and can be connected to a Steam Machine or other PC to stream games. It also comes with the critically acclaimed Half-Life: Alyx, but it doesn't come with a power supply. You can purchase one for $30 on Steam, but any Steam Deck charger or other USB-C charger that supports 45W or higher can work.

The Steam Frame comes in a 256 GB version and a 1 TB version. Here's how much each costs, according to the press release:

  • Steam Frame 256GB: 1,059 USD/ 1,529 CAD/ 1,049 EUR/ 889 GBP/ 1,609 AUD/ 4,539 PLN
  • Steam Frame 1TB: 1,299 USD/ 1,859 CAD/ 1,279 EUR/ 1,089 GBP/ 1,969 AUD/ 5,549 PLN 

And if you're wondering about the Steam Frame's other features or what games it might be able to run, here's the store page's rundown of the headset's hardware specs:

  • 4 nm Snapdragon® 8 Gen 3 - ARM64
  • 16GB Unified LPDDR5X RAM
  • 256GB UFS storage, microSD card slot
  • Rechargeable 21.6 Wh Li-ion battery
  • 2160 x 2160 LCD (per eye)
  • 72-144Hz refresh rate (144Hz experimental)
  • Inside-out camera based tracking
  • Wi-Fi 7, 2x2 - wireless adapter included
  • Bluetooth 5.4
  • Dual speaker drivers per ear, dual microphone array
  • SteamOS 3

You can sign up to order the Steam Frame and read about the rest of its specs here. For more details and some footage of the headset in action, you can check out the video below:

Alongside the Steam Frame, you can also purchase the ergonomic accessories kit for an extra $59 USD. It includes a strap for each controller, a top strap for the headset, and an extended light blocker. Valve describes the kit as "designed for comfort during extended play sessions." You can check out a breakdown of the accessories in the video below:

You can sign up to get a Steam Frame today, but don't forget that sign-ups end at 1:00 PM ET on September 17. If you want to learn more about the Steam Frame's launch game, check out our review of Half-Life: Alyx.

item.title: Everything Announced At The BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony
item.description:
BlizzCon 2026 kicks off today, and its Opening Ceremony contain tons of news about the company's catalog of games. Whether massively multiplayer, single-player, in cards or through an open world, this was a surprisingly announcement-filled Opening Ceremony.

Here's everything Blizzard announced at BlizzCon 2026.

Heroes of the Storm Adds Xal'atath

Though Blizzard slowed development on its crossover MOBA Heroes of the Storm a while back, Heroes of the Storm returned today with a new update. Xal'atath, the big baddie from World of Warcraft, is taking to the field on September 28. And Blizzard teases that more could be on the way, too. Maybe Heroes of the Storm isn't on the back-burner any longer?

Netflix x Diablo

Emphasizing that the company is Blizzard Entertainment, an animated Diablo series was confirmed to be in development with Netflix. No details were given beyond that, but there was a tease for other properties being an option for adaptations as well.

A StarCraft open-world shooter aims for 2030

The universe of StarCraft is back, this time through an open-world shooter currently dubbed StarCraft. Led by former Far Cry lead Dan Hay, the open-world shooter got a cinematic trailer showing off the vibe, which was fittingly grim. Currently, the team is targeting a 2030 launch, which feels just a bit far off, to say the least. But hey, it's nice to see StarCraft back.

Overwatch Adds Doctrine To The Roster

A new hero is joining the roster of Overwatch: the stylish and vampiric Doctrine. This Support arrives for a limited Hero Trial from September 12 through 14, before his official unlock in Season 5.

Diablo IV Comes To Switch 2

As part of the new season of Diablo IV, dubbed the Age of Hatred, numerous announcements were made for the dungeon-crawling and looting RPG. A new season is on the way, and with it, a Switch 2 version, out on September 15. (Reports have emerged of physical copies already showing up in stores today.)

Diablo V Is On The Way

Diablo V has been officially revealed for spring 2029. Diablo has taken Sanctuary, and there are no towns or safe havens left, which the Diablo team says will change how you approach the game. More will be discussed at a specific Diablo V panel, but it looks like the dungeon crawl will continue unabated.

Hearthstone Gets A New Expansion, And New Class 

Blizzard's Warcraft card game is getting a new expansion called Reign Of The Black Empire, themed around the old gods of Warcraft's universe. A new mechanic will let you piece together keywords onto a single card, mixing and matching card text to make devastating new effects. Battlegrounds will get Aberrations as well, adding some old god flavor to the auto-battler, and more lore is being dumped into the card game through the Journal. Some more experimental updates are on the way as well, including a new Tavern Brawl that allows for 2v2 Hearthstone.

On top of that, Hearthstone is getting its first new class in quite some time: the Monk.  Coming March 2027, the Pandaren Monk should bring some interesting new flavor to the current lineup of classes.

World of Warcraft Teases Both Midnight Eclipse And The Last Titan

The Worldsoul saga continues apace, as Xal'atath's schemes appear to be coming to fruition. In a new cinematic, Xal'atath gains access to the Worldsoul, which seems like a pretty bad thing for anyone living on the world. Midnight Eclipse, the next update for World of Warcraft, will presumably task players with trying to put a stop to all this.

When it comes to the next expansion, The Last Titan, Blizzard plans to bring a big chapter to close while also laying the groundwork for the road ahead. We did get a brief cinematic teaser, showing very, very large beings walking through the frozen wastes. The Last Titan is aiming for 2027.

Warcraft III: Reforged Gets A New Campaign Today

It's been how many years since we last got a new Warcraft III campaign? The Reforged edition of Warcraft III adds Forsaken Kingdom today, a new campaign set around the fall of Lordaeron, alongside a number of quality-of-life improvements. This includes some graphical upgrades and engine stuff, too. As a Warcraft III fan, this was pretty exciting for me. And even better, it's out today!

World of Warcraft Forever Arrives In November

Closing out the show, World of Warcraft's Holly Longdale stepped out to announce World of Warcraft Forever, a new re-envisioning of the classic MMORPG. You'll get to explore new zones like Mount Hyjal and the Riverglades, as well as expanded original zones. New raids, dungeons, reputations, skills and talents await in a new journey to 60.

Fresh combinations of races and classes will be available too, as well as a new race: the Skyborne. This massive update is set to arrive on November 4, with Beta opening on September 17.

That's all for BlizzCon 2026, a surprisingly large one. There's new content out today, in the near future, and in the far-off future too.

item.title: Warcraft III: Reforged Gets A New Campaign Today, Alongside New Graphics Mode
item.description:
Warcraft III is getting a new campaign for the first time in years. Forsaken Kingdom is a new campaign for Warcraft III: Reforged, arriving today alongside a number of improvements to the Reforged version of Warcraft III.

Set amid the fall of Lordaeron, a new prologue will detail the fallout after Arthas killed his father in the original Warcraft III campaign. Blizzard says the campaign will boast over 30 hours of gameplay, with some new gameplay additions and arriving alongside some big quality-of-life upgrades.

Notably, a new graphics mode is coming to Warcraft III: Reforged, which brings the overall look a little closer to the original direction for Warcraft III. 24-unit group selection and additional World Editor improvements are also part of the update. Plus, a new neutral hero in the Forsaken Paladin.

As someone who started following Blizzard thanks to its real-time strategy games, it's a pretty exciting update. Warcraft III: Reforged had some stumbles out of the gate, and seeing the ship get set upright is exciting. All that new content is out now for Warcraft III: Reforged owners.

item.title: Blizzard Announces World Of Warcraft: Forever, Expanding Vanilla WoW With New Zones, Raids, 1,000 New Quests Set
item.description:
Blizzard is rewinding the clock to 2004 and halting it there with World of Warcraft: Forever, a new game edition expanding the vanilla WoW experience with new and overhauled zones, 1,000 new quests spread across the entire 1–60 level bracket, 9 additional dungeons and 10-20 player raids, and a brand new neutral playable elven race: the Skyborne. Several new features include an SD/HD character toggle, new race and class combinations (the trailer below depicts an Undead Paladin), additional skills and talents, and new reputations to farm new items and account-wide perks. 

Three new zones include Mount Hyjal, Zephras Isle, and The Riverglades, and a new battleground takes place on Darkspear Islands. While Blizzard hasn't shared specifics yet about which zones are being overhauled, it's confirmed the engine features new lighting and global illumination, volumetric particle effects, a new water renderer, and real-time shadows. 

World of Warcraft: Forever Gameplay Trailer: 

A beta drops this Thursday, September 17, ahead of World of Warcraft: Forever's November 4 release date. In the meantime, additional details about the new game edition should surface throughout various panels happening at BlizzCon this weekend.

item.title: Blizzard Reveals StarCraft Open-World Shooter, Targeting 2030 Launch
item.description:
StarCraft is back, this time as an open-world shooter. During the BlizzCon 2026 keynote today, a new open-world shooter was announced, aiming for a 2030 release and simply called: StarCraft.

Dan Hay, previously a lead producer on the Far Cry series, to announce the new project and the team behind it. Hay said the crew plans to "re-ignite" the StarCraft universe, and brought a trailer to show exactly how.

The trailer is delightfully dark, featuring a Marine named Holt training up for the Dominion only to get run over by a Zergling rush when he touches down on a planet. Happens to the best of us. It also sounds like Mengsk shouting over the loudspeakers, and I'm curious to see what other little easter eggs are hiding in the trailer.

This is still a long-term plan, as Blizzard is currently targeting a 2030 launch. It also seems to simply be titled "StarCraft", which could cause some confusion down the line related to the RTS. But either way, it's neat to see StarCraft back. Now we'll just have to wait a few years to see what's in store for it.

item.title: Heroes Of The Storm Gets First New Character In Six Years, Arriving Later This Month
item.description:
During this morning's BlizzCon Opening Ceremony, Blizzard President Johanna Faries announced that Heroes of the Storm is getting its first new hero in six years. Xal'atath, World of Warcraft: Midnight's primary antagonist, is joining the Nexus as a ranged assassin, wielding her signature Void abilities. 

Xal'atath – Heroes of the Storm Trailer:

We've detailed Xal'atath's ability kit below, which was shared with Game Informer via a Blizzard press release:

  • Trait — Void Volley. Basic attacks build Soul Essence; at full Essence, unleash a barrage of void bolts at a target area while moving freely. Tied to the Void Whispers quest, which rewards range, faster charge, and piercing, empowered void damage as it progresses.
  • E — Dark Heart Ritual. Summon the Dark Heart talisman to pulse void energy at nearby enemies, then follow and detonate on any Shadow-Marked hero.
  • W — Void Step. Blink between three points in a triangular pattern, gaining attack damage at each stop; can be canceled early to reposition or escape.
  • Q — Shadow Mark. Cast a large Void Orb that marks heroes hit by its inner radius; the Dark Heart moves to the impact point and detonates on marked heroes.
  • Heroic — Void Eruption. Channel a growing void orb, launch it to blind enemies and dominate space, then detonate in a large area — cast on the Dark Heart for an instant, fully empowered eruption.
  • Heroic — Void Convergence. Summon a portal that spawns relentless void minions to overwhelm nearby enemies, replacing fallen minions until the portal ends or is destroyed.

"Thank you for believing in this game, for carrying the torch, and for reminding us sometimes - very loudly - what this game means to you," Blizzard President Johanna Faries said. "And who knows, we might even have another hero on the way in the near future. So stay tuned, and we'll see you in the Nexus."

item.title: Moss Developer Polyarc Is Shutting Down
item.description:
Polyarc, the developer best known for the acclaimed Moss series of VR and console games, has announced its closing its doors. This marks the end of the studio’s almost 12-year run.

On LinkedIn, Polyarc’s official profile posted this message:

“After nearly 12 years riding the joyous rollercoaster of emotions that is making video games, our time together has come to an end. As we wind down active development, we are saying our farewells to each other.

Working together over all of these years has been an honor. Bringing surprise and delight to those who played our games has been a privilege. Thank you to everyone at Polyarc, our work is now finished.”

The message concludes with a reverse recruiting spreadsheet with contact information for the studio's employees. 

Polyarc burst onto the scene with 2018’s Moss, an action-adventure puzzle game that shone as one of the more well-received VR titles of the time. It followed up with Moss: Book II in 2022. This July, Polyarc released Moss: The Forgotten Relic, a non-VR adventure combining both Moss games into a single title. 

Sadly, Polyarc isn’t the only studio to meet its end this year. Follow the links to read about the 2026 closures of Oxenfree developer Night School Studio, Wanderstop developer Ivy Road, Ubisoft's Halifax studio, and Demon's Souls remake makers Bluepoint Games.

item.title: The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – September 11, 2026
item.description:
This week was a surprisingly dense one for video game updates. Nintendo held two separate Direct presentations and Hideo Kojima is no longer working for PlayStation. This week also represents, however, a small reprieve for what continues to be an onslaught of new video games. Feel to catch your breath, but if you want to play some video games, you will find some ideas below after we take a look at some of the biggest stories of the week.

  • Marvel's Wolverine Review - Relentless Momentum
  • Everything Announced At The Zelda 40th Anniversary Nintendo Direct 
  • Every New Announcement At The September 2026 Nintendo Direct
  • Xbox Will Now Publish Hideo Kojima’s Action Espionage Game Physint After PlayStation Partnership Ends
  • The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Has Fully Voiced Cutscenes, A Jump Button, And Tons More
  • Halloween: The Game Review – Bespoke Boogeyman
  • Final Fantasy VII Revelation Preview  – Excitement For The Finale, Despite A Mediocre Demo

NHL 27

Brian Shea

Much of the excitement in the sporting world might be squarely focused on the start of the NFL season this weekend, but for hockey fans, it's hard not to look forward to the end of this month for the start of the NHL season. If you find yourself in that second camp, EA Sports' NHL 27 might be a solid way to scratch that itch while you wait for the real players to take the ice. Our reviewer wasn't the biggest fan of the AI-aided commentary, nor did he feel the game evolves over last year's title in meaningful ways, but the base gameplay is solid enough that those who are just looking to play some virtual hockey with the latest rosters can jump in and have a fun enough time.

You can read Game Informer's NHL 27 review at the link.

SlashZero Demo

Marcus Stewart
Boasting slick action and stylish visuals, SlashZero is an action roguelike sidescroller to keep on your radar. The game was announced during the PlayStation State of Play Japan showcase last week and has a free (but limited-time) demo on PS5 and Steam that you can try ahead of its full launch next year. I recommend checking it out. Featuring two playable characters, a swordsman and a gunslinger, you'll leap and blast your way through multiple timelines in a cyberpunk world. The fluid action and platforming rock, the anime-inspired visuals look sharp, and the time-traveling premise is intriguing. The fact that developer Streetlamp Studio has several more months to polish this already strong sample is exciting.

Halloween: The Game

Kyle Hilliard

Halloween: The Game, from Illfonic the creators of many nostalgic asymmetrical multiplayer games based on horror films, is pretty fun... as long as you go in with proper expectations for the genre.

In his review for the game, Wesley LeBlanc wrote, "Halloween needs some massaging. There are bugs galore, its Civilian onboarding isn’t great, and leveling up to unlock new color tints on sunglasses, or a new shirt or hat, isn’t the best motivation. But when I’m actually in a match, all of that fades away. The bugs aren’t game-breaking and blend in with IllFonic’s feature-not-a-bug jank, like one where another player and I hilariously moonwalked when we ran instead of sprinted. Learning what to do as a Civilian doesn’t take too much time, even without any helpful context built in-game, and cosmetics don’t affect how I play. What matters in Halloween is the scares I’m delivering and receiving, and the joy I’m feeling through it all. Death has arrived in IllFonic’s latest, and while the fear is abundant, so too is the fun waiting in the sleepy little town of Haddonfield."

Wes also makes clear in his review that while there is a single-player campaign, and it is a functional tutorial for the multiplayer game, that the multiplayer is the draw. If you're looking for a single-player Halloween game, this isn't it.

Meccha Chameleon on Switch 2

Kyle Hilliard

If you're not a big PC gamer, Meccha Chameleon is the game you probably heard about that sold a million billion copies. Its success will be intensely analyzed for the next few years by people who proclaim themselves experts on the business of video games on LinkedIn, but don't actually engage with video games as a form of artistic expression. Please look forward to their consulting efforts selling video game publishers the wrong lessons about Meccha Chameleon for years to come.

But with those details out of the way and for those who like to play video games because they are fun (and read sites like gameinformer.com because they are very smart), Meccha Chamelon is available now on Switch 2 and it's a great fit. The game is essentially high stakes hide and seek where players hide by literally painting themselves into the environment. With a group of friends, it can be a goofy blast. Just get ready to use your mouse on Switch 2 as it will make the painting aspect of the game much more fun.

Mewgenics

Charles Harte

I'll openly admit that I don't care much for Mewgenics' humor and aesthetics (and I mentioned as much in my review), but I can't deny that its game design is a work of beauty. You start each run with four cats, each with different stats and quirks, and assign them a class, equip them with items, and take them into a tactical roguelike run. There are so many variables in any given encounter that each new session is ripe with emergent gameplay, and you'll have crazy stories about the way your cats combo or clash with certain enemy types, equipment, and the environment. This week, it's finally made its way to consoles, so if you've been interested, now's as good a time as any to check it out.

Crisis Core: Final Fantasy VII Reunion on Switch 2

Kyle Hilliard

Crisis Core: Final Fantasy VII was originally released on PSP in 2007 and was generally well-liked. In terms of the Final Fantasy VII spin-offs that have been released over the years, this prequel is widely considered to be the best. In 2022, the game was updated and released for just about every contemporary platform at the time, and this week, it was released for Switch 2.

I reviewed the PlayStation 5 version of the game in 2022 and wrote, "Reunion is a well-executed remake of the 2007 game that delivers fun combat alongside a stilted story with an interesting and narratively important final act. If you plan on starting or continuing the Final Fantasy VII Remake journey, make sure to do your homework." The game is not necessary to enjoy the ongoing Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy, but it provides some nice context, and the action is pretty good, if a little repetitive. Mainly, I recommend it if you just want to investigate every corner of the Final Fantasy VII universe, especially if you've like to do as much as you can before Final Fantasy VII Revelation releases in April of next year.

Tabletop Pick – Dungeons & Dragons Arcana Unleashed and Arcana Unleased: Deadfall

Charles Harte

Next Tuesday, two new D&D books will be available for the general public: Arcana Unleashed and Arcana Unleashed: Deadfall. Technically, they've been in the wild for a while now, as they've been available at local game stores since September 1, and they were on sale at Gen Con before that. Still, I've been enjoying both. Arcana Unleashed is particularly exciting, with new subclasses, spells, and magic items that I'm definitely incorporating into my ongoing campaign. I'm most excited about the long-overdue update to the arcane archer and the new familiar-themed feats. I feel like every table I play at has a new person hoping to adopt a magic pet, and this makes it super easy, regardless of your class.

Meanwhile, Deadfall is a high-level (11-20) adventure ideal for a magic-heavy party. It's cool to see support for a campaign that starts so highly-leveled, especially since most tables never play long enough to experience it. Aside from a few magic items, there's not much in Deadfall that reaches the universal appeal of something like Arcana Unleashed, though. Regardless, the D&D team is still killing it with the art in these books, and they're a joy to leaf through whether or not I'll have time to play them any time soon.

item.title: Level-5’s Futuristic Detective RPG Decapolice Will Now Launch In 2027
item.description:
Level-5’s long-awaited detective game Decapolice has a new launch date, pushing it out of its previously announced 2026 window. The game is now coming in 2027 and has a new trailer showing it off in action.

Decapolice was announced in 2023 but has been repeatedly delayed. It stars Harvard Marks, a young detective and leader of the Special Investigation Unit’s rookie team. Marks, alongside fellow SIU members such as his friend and negotiation specialist Carl Oxford, must solve mysteries in the crime-ridden metropolis of Broadstone by visiting a virtual world counterpart called Decasim. This simulated world is a perfect copy of Broadstone but contains memories of past crimes that Marks must uncover to solve mysteries and bring criminals to justice. Sometimes Decasim’s data can be altered, changing the physical appearance of its inhabitants, such as turning Marks into a cat mascot, as seen in the new trailer. 

Gameplay consists of inspecting recreated crime scenes in Decasim to solve mysteries, both story and optional, in the real world. This involves managing evidence on a case board, profiling and accusing suspects, and confronting criminals. When facing suspects, you can either talk them into surrendering or, if that fails, face them in turn-based combat encounters after they transform into monsters called Crime Beasts. To this end, Level-5 has partnered with Scrap, a developer behind puzzle/escape games such as Do Not Play, to help develop Decapolice's case concepts. 

Decapolice will be available on PlayStation 5, Switch 2, and PC when it arrives next year. For more Level-5 news, it’s upcoming Professor Layton and the New World of Steam got a December launch date during yesterday’s Nintendo Direct.

item.title: Xbox Will Now Publish Hideo Kojima’s Action Espionage Game Physint After PlayStation Partnership Ends
item.description:
Physint, Kojima Productions’ upcoming stealth espionage game, will no longer be published by PlayStation. The console publisher has ended its collaboration on the game; meanwhile, Xbox, which is publishing Kojima’s upcoming horror game OD, has stepped in as Physint’s new publisher. 

Physint was first announced in January 2024 as Kojima Productions head Hideo Kojima’s return to action espionage. Kojima is, of course, the creator and primary creative mind of Konami’s Metal Gear series, one of the premier stealth action franchises. Little is known about Physint beyond the supporting cast, which includes actors Charlee Fraser (Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga, Anyone But You), Ma Dong-seok AKA Don Lee (Train to Busan, Eternals), and Minami Hamabe (Godzilla Minus One). Kojima has yet to reveal Physint's protagonist. 

A social media post by PlayStation states that “After careful consideration, we have made the difficult decision to step away from collaborating with Kojima Productions on its project Physint. We continue to have great admiration for Hideo Kojima’s vision for the game.

"Our relationship remains strong after three decades of industry-leading, genre-defining creative cooperation, and we look forward to continued close collaboration with Hideo Kojima and his award-winning independent studio in the future.”

As PlayStation mentioned, the company has a long history of publishing Kojima's work. Most recently, it served as the publisher for Kojima Productions' two Death Stranding games, the most recent of which launched last year.

Subsequently, Xbox released a statement announcing itself as Physint's new publisher. Its message reads:

Hideo Kojima has spent his career challenging conventions and expanding what games can be. Today, Kojima Productions announced the next chapter of its partnership with Xbox. 

"Creators have choices about where and how they bring their ideas to life. We’re honored that Kojima-san has chosen Xbox to work with Kojima Productions on Physint. His ambition to challenge conventions reflects the kind of creativity we want to support at Xbox,” said Asha Sharma, Xbox CEO

“This expands our relationship with Xbox beyond OD. As we move forward with the development of Physint we remain committed to redefining the action-espionage genre for players around the world,” said Hideo Kojima, game creator and founder of Kojima Productions. 

In addition to OD and Physint, this relationship will also extend beyond games, with Xbox and Kojima Productions collaborating across film and television to bring new stories to broader audiences. 

We look forward to sharing more as development progresses.

Hideo Kojima stated in May 2025 that Physint was likely 5-6 years away from release, positioning it as a next-generation title. With this move, the game will likely launch for Xbox’s upcoming console, Project Helix. Physint is slated to launch after OD, Kojima's upcoming horror game being developed in collaboration with filmmaker Jordan Peele and published by Xbox.

item.title: A Bunch Of Steam Achievements May Have Leaked For Games Like Persona 6, Kingdom Hearts 4, And More
item.description:
Steam achievements for a wide swath of upcoming and even announced games have seemingly leaked from Valve's backend. As a result, there might be massive spoilers floating around on the internet now for games like Persona 6, Persona 4 Revival, Kingdom Hearts IV, Mega Man: Dual Override, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3, Gears of War: E-Day, Kena: Scars of Kosmora, Silent Hill: Townfall, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, Stranger Than Heaven, and a lot more. 

We're not going to reveal any of the details you could learn from viewing these achievements, but know that there's a lot out there you could be spoiled on. As for how this happened, that remains unclear. The achievements appeared on Exophase, a site that uses APIs to automatically scan and display things like public Steam achievements. The site's owner, x3sphere, posted on ResetEra (view at your own risk) and explained how this might have happened. 

In response to someone saying, "There's a lot of in-development lists, placeholder achievements, etc. Something has gone catastrophically wrong on Steam's end it would seem," x3sphere said, "Yes I am the owner of the site [Exophase] and this is what appears to have happened. Seems like a possible screw up on Valve's end, a bunch of games with achievements that should be private are accessible through the API right now and that's why they got scanned into the site. I usually never see games without an actual name pop up with achievements, yet over the past hour or so a bunch have (when there's an unknown name, we just set it to the AppID). 

All of that sounds pretty legitimate, but leaked achievements for games like Persona 6 and Kingdom Hearts IV, for example, call into question the credibility of the achievements themselves. Those games are months and months away, if not longer – it seems strange that achievements for them are already uploaded into Steam's backend, but it's possible. 

All of this is to say that there are very likely big spoilers out there for games you might be looking forward to, so take caution when perusing social media, forums, YouTube, and the like.

item.title: Magic: The Gathering's Upcoming Reality Fracture Set Promises Multiversal Fun With 'What If?' Mechanics And Cards In Every Booster
item.description:
Reality Fracture is the next Magic: The Gathering set, and it's launching worldwide on October 2. It's centered around Jace Beleren, a legendary Planeswalker who knows the Multiverse is awry and needs to be fixed at its core. To do so, he will attempt to build an entirely new multiverse, piece by piece, forged in his own image, called the Echoverse, and this set will be themed around all the "What If?" scenarios that might appear as a result. 

Game Informer got an early look at the set from the designers at Wizards of the Coast, learning more about how the team is taking existing mechanics and doing some "wild things" to turn them on their head as part of Reality Fracture. Plus, we have new looks at upcoming cards and details on boxed product and more that will hit your local game store soon. 

Everything We Learned About Magic: The Gathering – Reality Fracture

"[Jace's] Echoverse, a perfected, mirror reality, is at the heart of Reality Fracture," according to the team behind this set. "As it threatens to consume the Multiverse we know, Jace's former allies must rise up against him. Welcome to Reality Fracture, where Jace's solution is everyone's problem. [...] Jace's former allies have teamed up to put a stop to his plan, allying with a certain Wildspeaker from Magic's past." And you can read the finale to this ten-episode story that's been unfolding as part of The Magic Story Podcast on Friday, Sept. 11. 

To emphasize the set's "What If?" theming, you'll find that mechanics like Amass, for example, which usually makes a creature token an army token, will instead make a Planeswalker token (specifically a Jace Planeswalker token). I mention Jace because Wizards of the Coast says Jace will now show up in almost every single limited game, noting that "it's a really impactful mechanic" that's key to Reality Fracture. That "What If?" theming continues throughout the set, even into the makeup of booster packs. In every booster pack, you will find the same character twice, but in different colors. You might open a pack and find both a red Chandra and a blue Chandra, and the Echoverse version of Chandra will have a special watermark on it indicating it's the "altered reality" version of the card. Another example is that you might open a pack with a Way of the Pyromancer card and a Way of the Cryomancer card as the "altered reality" version; the same goes for Return to the Light Realms sorcery and Rise of the Dark Realms sorcery. 

 

Despite the "altered reality" versions, Wizards of the Coast says it has learned from previous Multiverse-esque releases, and in Reality Fracture, the color pie stays true throughout.

item.title: Danganronpa 2x2 Kickstarts The Slayhem In January
item.description:
A new release date has been discovered! After a delay out of 2026, Danganronpa 2x2 is now set for a January 14, 2027 release.

For those at home who might not be familiar, Danganronpa is a series where several "Ultimates" — students at the top of their respective fields, be it sports, writing, hacking, or even delinquency — are trapped, and told they can either live out their lives together in their new home or escape, by killing another resident and getting away with the crime in the ensuing Class Trial.

Danganronpa 2x2 is a remix of Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair, where the Ultimates are trapped on the tropical Jabberwock Island. It is a very, very good entry, with some of my favorite trials in the series, and this "reboot" looks to not just enhance the experience, but add onto it.

Slayhem Mode is a new scenario with the same characters and setting, but a new set of trials and challenges to overcome. The trailer teases "Slayhem items," and it seems like a single incident will up-end the original structure of Danganronpa 2 and unleash a new sequence of events.

It's been a little while since the last official Danganronpa game, and while creator Kazutaka Kodaka has been very busy making other games (including my 2025 GOTY The Hundred Line: Last Defense Academy), he is involved with this update as well, which should bode well.

We'll see how the Slayhem unfolds when Danganronpa 2x2 arrives on January 14, 2027.
